reviews.title: Tide times are wrong
reviews.text:
I live on the Cumbrian west coast. I wanted an app that gave me widgets and watch functionality. This app fits the bill and I was prepared to pay a subscription for it BUT the tide times are over 30 minutes out when compared to 3 other paid apps and admiralty tables. 
Sorry. This is a deal breaker!!

reviews.title: Where are you getting your UK data from?!
reviews.text:
Edit: 23FEB2024

You have previously resolved the issues with Uk data but the Apple Watch complication doesn’t show the correct tidal chart information (check Burseldon and Warsash as two locations - these should have double high tides and they show a standard single high tide at the wrong time)

You took notice of the below and resolved it. However the latest update seems to have reintroduced this error. Can you please correct the source of the tidal info in the UK?

I have recently downloaded this app and bought a subscription only to find that the data you use to show UK tides and tide datum are incorrect. I live on the south coast of the uk where we have the unusual phenomenon of a double high tide. The major tidal points show this phenomenon but the more minor ones do not even though data is availed for these. In addition the tide tables used show not only the wrong times but also the wrong depths, by a significant and potential ship wrecking error. Take Southampton in the UK. On the 28NOV23, you show HT at 0821 at 2.1m. Double high tide at 1124 at 2m. The actual data for this day should read; 1119 at 4.59m with double high tide at 1304 at 4.56m This error is reflected across all the tidal stations across the Solent. I haven’t checked other parts of the UK. This needs correcting ASAP. If anyone relies on your tidal data then the potential for accidents is extremely high

reviews.title: No Family Sharing
reviews.text: I chose this app in part because the App Store indicates the app supports family sharing. There is no aspect of this app that does that, as far as I can tell. I wrote to Tide Guide twice to ask for confirmation whether the app supports family sharing, and I received no response. This app is not special enough to warrant the subscription fee if not shared.

reviews.title: Dangerously inaccurate
reviews.text:
It is up to 2m wrong compared to the UK Admiralty tides and 40 minutes or more out on time. I had planned to use it for planning my rowing schedule, but this level of inaccuracy is dangerous, potentially leaving my rowers unable to get ashore for hours until the next tide. I tried contacting the developer several times but had no reply. I can see that it gets some things right if you go to the data via a certain route, but go to the same data via a different route and it is wrong. Reporting tides 2m higher than the highest tide would be over the sea defences and flooding the town.
Location = Burnham on Sea, Bristol Channel, UK (second highest tides in the world). NB I have a degree in oceanography so I actually know a bit about tides.  Before making this criticism I compared it to the previous Android tides app I used and the UK Admiralty (based only a few miles from me) over several weeks of data to make sure it was not an error or aberration on my part.

reviews.title: Great app, but some incorrect data
reviews.text:
The data for my port is wildly inaccurate - taking an example of a week, it is out by up to 35 mins and almost 2m. The data is correct if I go to the map and select the port, but that is only for today.
I have contacted the developer with the evidence including the comparison data for a week against the UK Hydrographic Office, but have received no response.
Since the reason I bought the app was to plan when my gig rowers can go out safely, this app is not only useless but dangerous - we have the second highest tides in the world and errors could risk my rowers being unable to get back safely until the next tide. I don’t write this lightly, but every couple of years we do get someone drowned (thankfully not my rowers).
I gave the developer chance to respond privately, but I did not even get an acknowledgement.

So I recommend that you check carefully the predicted tides against another source before relying on them. It could just be it is my port that is in error (Burnham-on-Sea, UK) or. The problem might be more widespread.

reviews.title: Too many discrepancies to be reliably useful
reviews.text: I have this installed on iPad iPhone and Apple watch. There seems to be a consistent, over 1 hour inaccuracy shown on the Watch data, and more often than not on the iPhone Data. For some reason it seems more accurate on iPad app. Can’t figure out whats going on? Bottom line is…the Data can’t be relied upon which is a shame… the App would be fantastic if it was accurate and reliable. I’m on the west Coast of Scotland and use other data for comparison, including Admiralty Tide data. Please fix it

reviews.title: Wrong in UK
reviews.text: Beautiful and intuitive display, but the information is so often wrong or contradictory within the app that it’s unusable. If the data was accurate and the correct data for the location displayed, this would be fantastic

reviews.title: Nice app but very slow
reviews.text:
Layout and data display is good, but the Mac app is very, very slow. If I cmd-tab to the app it takes 2-3 seconds to come to the front and populate data. Every other app is instant. Perhaps it’s an electron app or something? 

Also no sync between iPhone, iPad and Mac apps so locations added to one are not shared. 

And no way to save locations or order them in the sidebar apart from recents which disappear after a while…

reviews.title: Zero Support
reviews.text: App no longer shows up on Watch. Fails to install on watch from App Store. App is not in the list of Available Apps under the Watch app on iPhone. iPhone and Watch have been reset. I reached out to support on 11/30/25 and still have no response.

reviews.title: Accessibility
reviews.text: Hello. Lovely app but it’s not fully accessible. Please ensure WCAG compliance, add better voiceover support and landscape support. This will allow more people to benefit from the insights and be included.
